basis: Independent contemporary French telegram39 identifies those formations. Other consequences include AMJJ→22 and RIRJY→RIR21.
The simultaneous unit identifications are rawJJ8→226, rawX8→16.Ldw., rawJX4→218, raw45→89, and raw82→63.
The French telegram39 lists226th Infantry,16th Landwehr,218th Infantry and89th Infantry; its303rd Division also matches the repeated digit pattern in raw2L2 if middleL is a separate garble.

The63rd corps reading agrees with the independently edited p163 parts15/18, themselves carrying an explicit historical digit assumption and editorial completion. This corroboration is conditional, not a new cipher-only proof of63.
The contemporary French list itself prints "89e D.I.?". The 89th Division identification, and therefore baseline5→9, is weaker and remains tentative even within this contextual hypothesis.
A display convention: read the repeated rawY separator label as canonicalX. It does not prove that the historical encipherer literally usedX.

The rawBA7R abbreviation and the proposed LIVAZEN7 place spelling both support ordinary-letterY. The sourceC→Z place repair is separately counted. This is a lexical inference, not an independently printed key.

The unchanged raw p230 A4 QUART abbreviation has Q at plaintext position80 (one-based), cellDF, from source coordinates10 and96. The neighboring HEUPT-to-HAUPT repair does not change this Q. Reading the abbreviation as Quartier supports Q as an ordinary letter; this is a separate lexical assumption, not part of the historical numeric map.

historical_source.caveat: The French intelligence telegram is contemporary evidence, not a proof of every formation identification in a later German message.
